edges.variation: The Mahabharata (3.188–189) links him less explicitly to Vishnu than the Puranas do.

edges.label: Kalki will destroy Kali, the personified spirit of the dark age
edges.variation: The personal battle with Kali is from the late Kalki Purana; earlier texts speak of destroying the wicked in general.

edges.label: In the Kalki Purana Shiva gives Kalki his white horse, a sword and a parrot
edges.variation: Kalki Purana only.

edges.label: The Kalki Purana says Kalki will marry Padmavati, an incarnation of Lakshmi
edges.variation: Kalki Purana only.

edges.label: The Bhagavata counts the four Kumaras collectively as the first avatar of Vishnu
edges.variation: Bhagavata Purana 1.3.6; they are not among the Dashavatara.

edges.label: The four Kumaras were the first mind-born sons of Brahma
The Kumaras cursed the Vaikuntha gatekeeper Jaya to be born among asuras for barring their way
The Kumaras cursed the Vaikuntha gatekeeper Vijaya to be born among asuras for barring their way
Sanatkumara teaches Narada the knowledge of the infinite (bhuman) in the Chandogya Upanishad
Sanatkumara instructed King Prithu in the knowledge of the Self
edges.variation: Bhagavata Purana 4.22.

edges.label: Nara and Narayana, twin sages of Badari, are an avatar of Vishnu
edges.variation: Bhagavata 1.3.9 counts them as one avatar; some traditions treat Nara as a separate figure.

edges.label: Arjuna is the sage Nara reborn, according to the Mahabharata
Krishna is the sage Narayana reborn, according to the Mahabharata
edges.variation: Other texts see Krishna as the full descent of Vishnu rather than of the sage Narayana.

edges.label: Narayana created Urvashi from his thigh (uru) to shame the apsaras Indra had sent to tempt him
edges.variation: Bhagavata 11.4 and other Puranas; in the Rig Veda Urvashi is an apsaras without this origin.

edges.label: Narada visited Nara-Narayana at Badari and received the Pancharatra teaching of the Narayaniya
The Narayaniya tells of a battle at Badari in which Narayana seized Rudra by the throat, darkening it
edges.variation: Mahabharata Shanti Parva (Narayaniya); the battle ends in reconciliation, and Shaiva texts explain Shiva's blue throat by the halahala poison.

edges.label: Indra, fearing their austerities, sent apsaras to disturb Nara-Narayana, and was humbled
Kapila is counted among Vishnu's avatars (Bhagavata 1.3.10); the Ramayana calls him Vasudeva
edges.variation: Classical Sankhya's Kapila is a human founder-sage; the identification with Vishnu is epic-Puranic.

edges.label: Kapila is the son of the sage Kardama
edges.variation: Bhagavata Purana 3.24.

edges.label: Kapila is the son of Devahuti
edges.variation: Bhagavata Purana 3.24.

edges.label: Kapila taught his mother Devahuti Sankhya and the path of devotion, leading to her liberation
Kapila's fiery glance burned to ashes the sixty thousand sons of King Sagara, who accused him of stealing the sacrificial horse
edges.variation: The target of the fire was Sagara's sons, not the king himself.

edges.label: Kapila returned the sacrificial horse to Anshuman and foretold that Ganga's waters would redeem his ancestors
Indra stole Sagara's sacrificial horse and left it beside the meditating Kapila
edges.variation: Bhagavata 9.8 and other Puranas name Indra as the thief; the Ramayana speaks only of a disguised thief.

edges.label: Dattatreya is counted among Vishnu's avatars (Bhagavata 1.3.11)
edges.variation: Later tradition venerates him as the combined incarnation of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva.

edges.label: Datta and Nath traditions revere Dattatreya as embodying Shiva as well as Vishnu and Brahma
edges.variation: The Bhagavata makes Durvasa the portion of Shiva; the Trimurti Dattatreya is a medieval development.

edges.label: Dattatreya is the son of the sage Atri
Dattatreya is the son of Anasuya, famed for her chastity
Dattatreya and Durvasa were born to Atri and Anasuya as portions of Vishnu and Shiva
Soma was born to Atri and Anasuya as Brahma's portion, alongside Dattatreya
edges.variation: Bhagavata 4.1; elsewhere Soma is born from Atri's eyes or from the churning of the ocean.

edges.label: Dattatreya granted Kartavirya Arjuna a thousand arms, a golden chariot and sovereignty
The Bhagavata says Dattatreya taught the knowledge of the Self to Alarka, Prahlada and others
The avadhuta who teaches King Yadu about his twenty-four gurus is identified with Dattatreya
edges.variation: Bhagavata 11.7–9 does not name him; the identification is traditional.

edges.label: In the Tripura Rahasya, Dattatreya instructs Parashurama in the knowledge of the Goddess Tripura
edges.variation: Tripura Rahasya, a Shakta text of uncertain date.

edges.label: Yajna, the personified sacrifice, is Vishnu's avatar in the Svayambhuva Manvantara
edges.variation: Bhagavata 1.3.12; the Vedic formula 'yajno vai vishnuh' underlies the identification.

edges.label: Yajna held the office of Indra during the first (Svayambhuva) Manvantara
edges.variation: Indra is treated as an office held by different beings in each Manvantara (Bhagavata 8.1).

edges.label: The Bhagavata counts Rishabha, the naked royal ascetic, among Vishnu's avatars
edges.variation: In Jainism Rishabhanatha is the first Tirthankara, a liberated human teacher, not an avatar.

edges.label: Jealous of Rishabha, Indra withheld the rains, which Rishabha restored by his own power; Indra later gave him his daughter Jayanti
edges.variation: Bhagavata Purana 5.4.

edges.label: The Bhagavata counts Prithu as a partial (amsha) avatar of Vishnu
edges.variation: He is described as an empowered portion rather than a full avatar; Vedic texts know him only as the first king.

edges.label: Prithu emerged when the sages churned the arm of the slain king Vena
edges.variation: This is not ordinary parentage; the dark Nishada came from Vena's thigh, Prithu from his arm.

edges.label: Prithu pursued the Earth, fleeing as a cow, until she agreed to yield her riches; she was named Prithvi after him
edges.variation: As she became like his daughter, the Earth took his name; the Vedic Prithvi is much older than this etymological legend.

edges.label: Indra repeatedly stole the horse of Prithu's hundredth ashvamedha, until Brahma persuaded Prithu to stop
edges.variation: Bhagavata Purana 4.19.

edges.label: Svayambhuva Manu served as the calf when Prithu milked the grains from the cow-Earth
edges.variation: Vishnu Purana 1.13, Bhagavata 4.18; other lists name a different calf.

edges.label: Vena descends from Dhruva through his father Anga
edges.variation: Genealogies differ in the intermediate generations.

edges.label: The sages struck down the impious Vena with mantra-charged blades of kusha grass
edges.variation: Most texts say simply 'the sages' (rishis, munis) without naming the Seven Sages specifically.

edges.label: Vena forbade the worship of Vishnu and sacrifices, demanding worship of himself
Dhanvantari, the divine physician, is counted among Vishnu's avatars (Bhagavata 1.3.17)
Vishnu promised Dhanvantari a second birth among men, a share of sacrifices and mastery of Ayurveda
edges.variation: Harivamsha 1.29.

edges.label: In the Sushruta Samhita, Indra teaches Ayurveda to Dhanvantari as Divodasa, king of Kashi
edges.variation: The Sushruta Samhita's lineage runs Brahma - Prajapati - Ashvins - Indra - Dhanvantari; the Kashi king may be distinct from the ocean-born god.

edges.label: Dhanvantari brought up the pot of amrita, which Mohini recovered from the asuras and served to the gods
Mohini is the enchanting female form of Vishnu (Bhagavata 1.3.17)
Mohini's discus severed Svarbhanu's head when he secretly drank the amrita, creating Rahu and Ketu
edges.variation: Most texts attribute the stroke to Vishnu; the asura survived as Rahu (head) and Ketu (body).

edges.label: Ketu is the headless body of the asura beheaded by Mohini's discus at the distribution of amrita
Mohini tricked Bhasmasura into placing his hand on his own head, burning himself to ashes
edges.variation: A popular South Indian folk and dance-drama tale absent from major Sanskrit Puranas; the Bhagavata 10.88 parallel (Vrikasura) has Vishnu appear as a young brahmachari.

edges.label: Shiva was overwhelmed by Mohini's beauty; Kerala tradition makes them parents of Ayyappa
edges.variation: Bhagavata 8.12 describes Shiva's infatuation but no marriage; the union is regional.

edges.label: In the Tamil Koothandavar tradition, Krishna as Mohini marries Aravan the night before his sacrifice
edges.variation: Tamil (Villiputtur Alvar and Koovagam) tradition; not in the Sanskrit Mahabharata.

edges.label: Mohini secured the amrita for Indra and the gods, restoring their strength
Hayagriva, the horse-headed lord of knowledge, is a form of Vishnu
edges.variation: Bhagavata 2.7.11 lists him; the Mahabharata Narayaniya calls him Hayashiras.

edges.label: Hayagriva slew the demon Madhu after recovering the stolen Vedas
edges.variation: In the Narayaniya, Vishnu slays Madhu in his usual form after Hayagriva recovers the Vedas; the Devi Mahatmya has Vishnu kill him at the Goddess's prompting.

edges.label: Hayagriva slew the demon Kaitabha after recovering the stolen Vedas
edges.variation: In the Narayaniya, Vishnu slays Kaitabha in his usual form after Hayagriva recovers the Vedas; the Devi Mahatmya has Vishnu kill him at the Goddess's prompting.

edges.label: Hayagriva recovered the Vedas stolen from Brahma and restored them to him
Hayagriva taught the Lalita Sahasranama and the glory of Lalita to the sage Agastya
edges.variation: Brahmanda Purana, Lalitopakhyana.

edges.label: Hayagriva is worshipped with Saraswati as a deity of learning; tradition holds he is her teacher
edges.variation: Sri Vaishnava devotional tradition (e.g. Vedanta Desika); not a Puranic narrative.

edges.label: Kala Bhairava, the terrifying form born from Shiva's wrath, is counted among Shiva's avatars
edges.variation: The Shiva Purana lists him among the avatars; many texts describe him as a form (murti) of Shiva.

edges.label: Bhairavi, one of the Mahavidyas, is the consort of Bhairava
In some Puranas Shiva as Bhairava impales the asura Andhaka on his trident
edges.variation: Kurma Purana; other texts have Shiva himself impale Andhaka, who repents and becomes the gana Bhringi.

edges.label: Tantric tradition pairs the eight Bhairavas with the eight Matrikas as guardians
Virabhadra, born of Shiva's wrath at Sati's death, is counted among Shiva's avatars
edges.variation: Mahabharata: born from Shiva's mouth; Bhagavata 4.5: from a lock of his matted hair.

edges.label: Bhadrakali accompanied Virabhadra in destroying Daksha's sacrifice
edges.variation: Some traditions regard her as his consort.

edges.label: At Daksha's sacrifice Virabhadra tore out the beard of the sage Bhrigu
edges.variation: Bhagavata 4.5.

edges.label: In some Shaiva Puranas Vishnu defends Daksha's sacrifice and fights Virabhadra
edges.variation: Shiva Purana and Kurma Purana; the Bhagavata has Vishnu absent from the fight.

edges.label: In the Vayu Purana, Devi (Uma) creates Bhadrakali from her anger at Daksha's insult to Shiva
Kerala tradition says Bhadrakali sprang from Shiva's third eye to slay the asura Darika
edges.variation: Kerala regional tradition (Darikavadham); she is sometimes called Shiva's daughter.

edges.label: Bhadrakali helped destroy Daksha's sacrifice
Sharabha, the eight-legged bird-beast, is a form of Shiva in Shaiva sectarian texts
edges.variation: Linga Purana, Shiva Purana; rejected by Vaishnava traditions.

edges.label: In the Linga Purana, Virabhadra assumes the Sharabha form
edges.variation: Linga Purana 1.96; the Shiva Purana has Shiva take the form directly.

edges.label: In Shaiva sectarian accounts Sharabha overpowered the raging Narasimha and humbled him
edges.variation: Sectarian: Shaiva texts say Narasimha was subdued (some say flayed) and merged back into Vishnu; Vaishnava traditions reject the story, some adding that Narasimha became Gandaberunda to defeat Sharabha.

edges.label: The Kalika Purana has Shiva as Sharabha subdue Varaha when the boar will not relinquish his form
edges.variation: Kalika Purana only; a Shakta-Shaiva sectarian narrative.

edges.label: Kirata is Shiva in the guise of a mountain hunter who tested Arjuna
edges.variation: The Mahabharata presents it as a disguise; the Shiva Purana counts it among Shiva's avatars.

edges.label: Pleased by Arjuna's valour in their duel, Shiva as Kirata granted him the Pashupata weapon
Arjuna and the hunter fought over a boar both had shot, until Arjuna recognised Shiva
Parvati accompanied Shiva in the hunt, disguised as a Kirata woman
Ayyappa is Hariharaputra, son of Shiva and Mohini (Vishnu's female form)
edges.variation: Regional Kerala tradition; not in the classical Sanskrit Puranas.

edges.label: Ayyappa slew the buffalo-demoness Mahishi, who could be killed only by a son of Shiva and Vishnu
edges.variation: Some accounts say Mahishi was freed from a curse and became Malikappurathamma.

edges.label: As Hariharaputra, Ayyappa embodies the union of Shiva (Hara) and Vishnu (Hari)
edges.variation: Ayyappa is their son rather than the Harihara form itself; the link is theological.

edges.label: Renuka was the wife of the sage Jamadagni
Enraged by Renuka's momentary lapse, Jamadagni ordered her death
edges.variation: Mahabharata 3.116; the order is a command to his sons rather than a verbal curse.

edges.label: In some regional traditions Renuka's severed head on another body becomes the goddess Matangi / Yellamma
edges.variation: Karnataka, Maharashtra and Andhra folk traditions; not in the Sanskrit texts.

edges.label: Kartavirya Arjuna defeated Ravana, bound him and held him captive in Mahishmati
The sage Pulastya persuaded Kartavirya Arjuna to release his grandson Ravana
Kartavirya Arjuna seized the sacrificial calf from Jamadagni's hermitage
edges.variation: Versions differ on whether he or his sons stole the calf or the cow, and on who killed Jamadagni.

edges.label: The Haihaya king Kartavirya Arjuna belongs to the lineage of Yadu
The sage Apava, identified with Vasishtha, cursed Kartavirya to be slain by Parashurama for burning his hermitage
edges.variation: Mahabharata 12.49; the identification of Apava with Vasishtha is traditional.

edges.label: Kardama married Devahuti, daughter of Svayambhuva Manu
Kardama was born from Brahma's shadow
edges.variation: Bhagavata 3.12; some Puranas make him a son of Pulaha.

edges.label: Kardama's austerities at Bindu Sarovara were rewarded by a vision of Vishnu, who promised to be born as his son
Anasuya, wife of Atri, was one of Kardama's nine daughters
edges.variation: Bhagavata 3.24; other Puranas make Anasuya a daughter of Daksha.

edges.label: Anasuya was a daughter of Devahuti
edges.variation: Bhagavata 3.24; other Puranas make Anasuya a daughter of Daksha.

edges.label: Arundhati, wife of Vasishtha, was one of Kardama's nine daughters
edges.variation: Bhagavata 3.24; other texts give different parentage.

edges.label: Arundhati was a daughter of Devahuti
edges.variation: Bhagavata 3.24; other texts give different parentage.

edges.label: Rama is the seventh avatar of Vishnu
edges.variation: Valmiki's Bala and Uttara Kandas state it explicitly; many scholars regard these books as later layers, the core narrative presenting Rama primarily as an ideal human hero.

edges.label: Krishna is the eighth avatar of Vishnu
edges.variation: Gaudiya Vaishnavas, following Bhagavata 1.3.28 ('krishnas tu bhagavan svayam'), hold Krishna to be the Supreme Lord himself, the source of all avatars.

edges.label: Balarama is counted as an avatar of Vishnu (Bhagavata 1.3.23)
edges.variation: Dashavatara lists vary: many include Buddha as the ninth avatar, while others (especially in South India) place Balarama there.

edges.label: Balarama is widely regarded as an incarnation of the serpent Shesha
edges.variation: The Mahabharata and Puranas describe a white hair of Vishnu (Balarama) and a black hair (Krishna); Shesha leaving Balarama's mouth at his death supports the Shesha identification.

edges.label: The Bhagavata counts the sage Narada among Vishnu's avatars (1.3.8)
edges.variation: Most texts treat Narada as a devotee and mind-born son of Brahma rather than an avatar.

edges.label: The Bhagavata counts Vyasa, compiler of the Vedas, among Vishnu's avatars (1.3.21)
edges.variation: Vishnu Purana 3.3–4 calls each age's Veda-arranger a form of Vishnu.

edges.label: Durvasa was born to Atri and Anasuya as a partial incarnation of Shiva
edges.variation: Bhagavata 4.1; other texts attribute his birth to Shiva's anger.

edges.label: The Mahabharata says Ashwatthama was born of the combined portions of Mahadeva, Yama, Kama and Krodha
edges.variation: A partial incarnation (amsha), not a full avatar.

edges.label: The sage Kashyapa fathered Hiranyakashipu on Diti
Hiranyakashipu was the father of Prahlada
Kayadhu was the mother of Prahlada (Prahrada Kayadhava)
Kayadhu, daughter of Jambha, was Hiranyakashipu's queen
Hiranyakashipu and Hiranyaksha were the twin sons of Diti
edges.variation: The Bhagavata calls Hiranyakashipu the elder; other tellings make Hiranyaksha the first conceived

edges.label: Holika was the sister of Hiranyakashipu (popular Holi tradition)
Hiranyakashipu swore vengeance on Vishnu for slaying his brother and banned his worship
Hiranyakashipu persecuted his own son for his devotion to Vishnu
Hiranyakashipu conquered Indra's heaven and ruled the three worlds
Hiranyakashipu was the first birth of Vishnu's doorkeeper Jaya, cursed by the Kumaras
edges.variation: The Bhagavata (3.16, 7.1) says Jaya and Vijaya became Hiranyakashipu and Hiranyaksha without assigning each individually; popular tradition pairs Jaya with Hiranyakashipu, some tellings reverse it

edges.label: Ravana was the rebirth of Hiranyakashipu, before his final birth as Shishupala (Vishnu Purana 4.15, Bhagavata 7.1)
Shukracharya was the preceptor of Hiranyakashipu's house; his sons taught Prahlada
Vatapi was Hiranyakashipu's grandson through Hlada (Bhagavata 6.18)
Ilvala was Hiranyakashipu's grandson through Hlada (Bhagavata 6.18)
Sunda, son of Nikumbha, was born in Hiranyakashipu's line (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Upasunda, son of Nikumbha, was born in Hiranyakashipu's line (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Kashyapa fathered Hiranyaksha on Diti at the inauspicious hour of dusk
Holika was the sister of Hiranyaksha and Hiranyakashipu (popular tradition)
Hiranyaksha challenged Varuna, who sent him to find Vishnu (Bhagavata 3.17)
Hiranyaksha was the first birth of the doorkeeper Vijaya, cursed by the Kumaras
edges.variation: The Bhagavata names the pair without an individual assignment; some tellings make Hiranyaksha the rebirth of Jaya

edges.label: Kumbhakarna was the rebirth of Hiranyaksha, the doorkeepers' second birth (Bhagavata 7.1)
Shiva granted the childless Hiranyaksha a son, the blind Andhaka (Shiva and Linga Puranas)
Hiranyaksha raised Andhaka, Shiva's son, as his adoptive son (Shiva Purana)
Narada taught Prahlada devotion while he was still in his mother's womb (Bhagavata 7.7)
Prahlada was the father of Virochana
Prahlada cursed his grandson Bali to lose his kingdom for slighting Vishnu
edges.variation: Vamana Purana only

edges.label: Prahlada granted a boon to Indra, disguised as a brahmin pupil, who asked for his virtue (shila) (Mahabharata, Shanti Parva)
Prahlada fought Nara-Narayana at Badari before becoming their devotee
edges.variation: Vamana Purana

edges.label: Holika tried to burn Prahlada on a pyre but was consumed herself
Narada sheltered the pregnant Kayadhu in his hermitage and instructed her (Bhagavata 7.7)
Indra seized the pregnant Kayadhu, meaning to kill her unborn child, until Narada intervened
Virochana was the father of Mahabali
Virochana and Indra were rival kings of asuras and devas, and fellow students of Prajapati
Banasura was the eldest of Bali's hundred sons
Bali surrendered everything to Vishnu and is honoured among his great devotees
Shukracharya was Bali's guru and led his sacrifices
Shukracharya cursed Bali to lose his fortune for giving Vamana the three paces against his advice (Bhagavata 8.20)
Banasura was the father of Usha, who fell in love with Aniruddha
Krishna severed all but four of Bana's arms and spared him at Shiva's request
Bana imprisoned Aniruddha with serpent-nooses for courting Usha
Kartikeya fought on Bana's side against Pradyumna (Bhagavata 10.63)
As sister of Hiranyakashipu, Holika is counted a daughter of Diti
edges.variation: Her parentage is implied by popular tradition, not stated in the major Puranas

edges.label: As sister of Hiranyakashipu, Holika is counted a daughter of Kashyapa
edges.variation: Her parentage is implied by popular tradition, not stated in the major Puranas

edges.label: Holika's immunity to fire is often said to be a boon from Brahma
edges.variation: Other tellings give her a fire-proof shawl or cloth instead

edges.label: In later texts both are sons of Tvashtr: Vritra was produced to avenge his brother Vishvarupa
In the Bhagavata, Vritra prays to Vishnu before his last battle and dies as a liberated devotee (Bhagavata 6.11)
Parvati cursed the Vidyadhara Chitraketu, who was reborn as Vritra (Bhagavata 6.17)
edges.variation: Bhagavata Purana only

edges.label: The Maruts accompanied and cheered Indra in the fight against Vritra (Rig Veda)
Vishvarupa served as priest of the devas and taught Indra the Narayana Kavacha (Bhagavata 6.8)
Indra and Namuchi swore a pact of friendship that Indra later circumvented (Shatapatha Brahmana 12.7.3)
Namuchi is a son of Kashyapa by Danu in epic genealogies
The Ashvins healed Indra after Namuchi drained his strength and helped defeat him (Rig Veda 10.131)
Pradyumna, stolen as an infant by Shambara, grew up and killed him (Bhagavata 10.55)
edges.variation: The Puranic sorcerer may be a different figure from the Vedic Shambara

edges.label: Rati, living in Shambara's house as Mayavati, raised Pradyumna and taught him the magic that defeated Shambara
The Angiras seers sang the rock of Vala open and freed the cattle of light
The Bhagavata (5.24) makes Bala, the later form of Vala, a son of Maya
edges.variation: Rests on the identification of the Vedic Vala with the Puranic Danava Bala

edges.label: Puloman is a son of Kashyapa by Danu
The newborn Chyavana's radiance burned the rakshasa Puloman who had abducted his mother Puloma (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 6)
edges.variation: This rakshasa Puloman may be a different being from Shachi's father

edges.label: Shukracharya (Ushanas Kavya) was a son of the sage Bhrigu
Shukracharya was the father of Devayani
Shukracharya taught Kacha the Mrita Sanjivani from inside his own belly (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Shukracharya cursed Yayati with old age for wronging Devayani with Sharmishtha (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Shukracharya worshipped Shiva with severe austerities
As the planet Shukra (Venus), he is one of the Navagraha
Maya was the father of Mandodari by the apsara Hema (Ramayana, Uttara Kanda)
Maya gave his daughter Mandodari to Ravana in marriage
Arjuna saved Maya from the Khandava fire; in return Maya gave him the conch Devadatta
Maya built the wondrous Maya Sabha for Yudhishthira at Indraprastha (Sabha Parva)
Maya brought Bhima a mighty mace from Lake Bindusara (Sabha Parva)
Maya built the three flying cities of Tripura for the asura brothers
Indra killed Maya with his vajra over the apsara Hema (Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda)
edges.variation: In the Mahabharata and Puranas Maya survives

edges.label: Maya was spared at the burning of Tripura for his devotion to Shiva
edges.variation: Shiva Purana and other Puranas

edges.label: Rahu (Saimhikeya) is the son of Simhika by the Danava Viprachitti (Bhagavata 6.18)
edges.variation: The Puranic Simhika, a daughter of Diti, is usually distinguished from the shadow-seizing demoness of the Sundara Kanda

edges.label: The Bhagavata's list of Danu's sons (6.6) includes Svarbhanu
edges.variation: Elsewhere he is Danu's grandson through Viprachitti and Simhika

edges.label: Rahu, the north lunar node, is one of the Navagraha
Atri recovered the Sun after Svarbhanu pierced it with darkness (Rig Veda 5.40)
Ketu is the headless body of the same asura Svarbhanu whose head became Rahu
Ketu, the south lunar node, is one of the Navagraha
Vishnu's discus severed Svarbhanu's body, which became Ketu
Krishna beheaded Naraka with his discus at Pragjyotisha (Bhagavata 10.59)
edges.variation: Many South Indian and Deepavali tellings give the fatal blow to Satyabhama

edges.label: Satyabhama, as an incarnation of Bhudevi, killed Naraka, who could die only by his mother's hand
edges.variation: Regional and later tradition; the Bhagavata has Krishna slay him with Satyabhama at his side

edges.label: Narakasura was the father of Bhagadatta, later king of Pragjyotisha
Naraka oppressed the gods; Indra appealed to Krishna to stop him
Naraka seized the royal umbrella of Varuna
Vasishtha cursed Naraka to die by Vishnu's hand after he barred the sage from Kamakhya (Kalika Purana)
Kamsa was Kalanemi reborn (Harivamsha; Bhagavata 10.1)
Kalanemi routed the devas and usurped their functions in the Tarakamaya war
Hanuman killed the rakshasa Kalanemi who, disguised as a hermit, tried to delay him (Adhyatma Ramayana)
edges.variation: Absent from Valmiki; this rakshasa is usually regarded as distinct from the Danava

edges.label: The rakshasa Kalanemi acted on Ravana's orders to stop Hanuman (Adhyatma Ramayana)
edges.variation: Refers to the later rakshasa Kalanemi, not the Harivamsha Danava

edges.label: Vatapi and Ilvala were brothers who killed brahmin guests with their feast trick
Agastya ate Vatapi in the form of a ram and digested him completely
Agastya burned Ilvala to ashes with his gaze (Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 11)
edges.variation: In the Mahabharata (Vana Parva) Ilvala survives and gives Agastya wealth

edges.label: Sunda and Upasunda were inseparable brothers, sons of Nikumbha
Sunda and Upasunda killed each other with maces in their quarrel over Tilottama
Upasunda and Sunda killed each other with maces in their quarrel over Tilottama
Tilottama was created to turn Sunda against his brother
Tilottama was created to turn Upasunda against his brother
Kali possessed Nala and made him gamble away his kingdom (Mahabharata, Vana Parva)
Damayanti's curse on the cause of Nala's misery tormented Kali within him
Karkotaka's venom, from biting Nala, burned the Kali possessing him
Parikshit subdued Kali and, when he surrendered, allotted him places to dwell (Bhagavata 1.17)
Duryodhana was born from a portion of Kali (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Madhu and Kaitabha were twin asuras born together on the cosmic ocean
Madhu sprang from the ear-wax of the sleeping Vishnu (Devi Mahatmya 1)
edges.variation: In the Narayaniya they arise from drops of water on the lotus

edges.label: The Goddess granted Madhu the boon of dying only when he chose (Devi Bhagavata 1)
edges.variation: Devi Bhagavata only

edges.label: Kaitabha sprang from the ear-wax of the sleeping Vishnu (Devi Mahatmya 1)
edges.variation: In the Narayaniya they arise from drops of water on the lotus

edges.label: The Goddess granted Kaitabha the boon of dying only when he chose (Devi Bhagavata 1)
edges.variation: Devi Bhagavata only

edges.label: Rambha fathered Mahisha on a she-buffalo (Vamana Purana, Devi Bhagavata)
Mahishasura defeated Indra and usurped the throne of heaven
In Kerala tradition Mahishi is Mahishasura's sister and avenger
edges.variation: Other Kerala tellings make her his cousin (daughter of Karambha) or his widow.

edges.label: The Kalika Purana makes Mahisha a devotee of Shiva who asks to stay forever at the Goddess's feet
edges.variation: Found in the Kalika Purana and regional tradition, not the Devi Mahatmya.

edges.label: Shumbha's slayer, called Ambika and Chandika in the Devi Mahatmya, is worshipped as Durga
edges.variation: The Devi Mahatmya's goddess is identified with Durga in later tradition.

edges.label: Nishumbha fell to the Goddess of the Devi Mahatmya, worshipped as Durga
edges.variation: The Devi Mahatmya calls her Ambika, Chandika and Devi.

edges.label: Shumbha and Nishumbha were brothers and joint rulers of the asuras
Brahma made Shumbha invulnerable to gods, men and beasts — but not to women (Devi Bhagavata)
Brahma's boon left Nishumbha vulnerable only to a woman (Devi Bhagavata)
Shumbha and Nishumbha seized Indra's realm and the gods' sacrificial shares
Chanda was Shumbha's servant and general, who first reported the Goddess's beauty
Munda was Shumbha's servant and general, who urged him to claim the Goddess
Raktabija was a great general in Shumbha's army
Dhumralochana was the first general Shumbha sent to seize the Goddess
Chanda and Munda are paired generals, called brothers in popular tradition
edges.variation: The Devi Mahatmya pairs them without stating kinship.

edges.label: Chanda and Munda led an army to seize the Goddess by force
Munda praised the Goddess to Shumbha and then marched to capture her
Deprived of Vedic offerings, Indra and the gods were powerless before Durgama
Brahma made Aruna immune to weapons, men, women and all two- and four-legged beings
Brihaspati persuaded Aruna to abandon the Gayatri, the source of his power
Aruna drove Indra and the gods from heaven
Taraka was the father of the Tripura brothers Tarakaksha, Kamalaksha and Vidyunmali
Taraka was Diti's grandson through her son Vajranga (Shiva Purana)
Taraka conquered heaven and made the gods his servants
Andhra tradition says Taraka wore a Shiva linga, whose shattered pieces are worshipped at the Pancharama shrines
edges.variation: Regional (Andhra) tradition.

edges.label: Shiva impaled Andhaka on his trident and held him aloft until he was purged of sin
edges.variation: In most versions Andhaka is not killed but redeemed and made a gana (Bhringi).

edges.label: Andhaka was born from Shiva's sweat when Parvati playfully covered his eyes (Shiva Purana)
edges.variation: Matsya, Kurma and Vamana Puranas make him Hiranyaksha's own son.

edges.label: Parvati's touch on Shiva's eyes brought Andhaka into being, so she is his mother (Shiva Purana)
edges.variation: Matsya, Kurma and Vamana Puranas make him Hiranyaksha's own son.

edges.label: Brahma's boon made Andhaka nearly invincible
Shukracharya revived Andhaka's fallen asuras with his secret lore until Shiva swallowed him
Nandi fought Andhaka's forces and carried Shukracharya off to Shiva
The redeemed Andhaka became Shiva's emaciated gana Bhringi
edges.variation: Elsewhere Bhringi is an independent sage who worshipped Shiva alone.

edges.label: Impaled and purified, Andhaka praised Shiva and became his devoted gana
Jalandhara's invincibility rested on the fidelity of his wife Vrinda
Shukracharya crowned Jalandhara king of the asuras and served as his preceptor
Jalandhara conquered heaven to avenge the gods' churning of his father, the Ocean
Both born of the ocean, Lakshmi regarded Jalandhara as her brother
edges.variation: Kinship through their common origin in the ocean (Shiva Purana).

edges.label: Rahu carried Jalandhara's demand for Parvati to Shiva
Jalandhara coveted Parvati and approached her disguised as Shiva
Vrinda was the daughter of the asura Kalanemi (Shiva Purana)
edges.variation: In the Tulasi version she is the daughter of King Dharmadhvaja.

edges.label: As Tulasi she is ritually wedded to Vishnu, as Shaligram, in the annual Tulasi Vivah
edges.variation: Ritual and later Puranic tradition; some celebrate her marriage to Krishna.

edges.label: As the Tulasi plant she is held dearest to Vishnu; no offering to him is complete without her leaves
edges.variation: In the Brahmavaivarta, Tulasi performs austerities to win Narayana as husband.

edges.label: The Brahmavaivarta and Devi Bhagavata call Tulasi a partial manifestation of Lakshmi
edges.variation: Applies to the Tulasi–Shankhachuda version, which tradition merges with Vrinda's.

edges.label: Vrika propitiated Shiva by offering his own flesh into the fire at Kedara
Vishnu, as a young brahmachari, tricked Vrika into touching his own head, which burst apart (Bhagavata 10.88)
Bhasmasura turned his boon on Shiva himself, chasing him across the worlds to seize Parvati
In the Taittiriya Samhita, Rudra shot the arrow that destroyed the asuras' three forts
edges.variation: Vedic version: the arrow is made of Agni, Soma and Vishnu; the named brothers appear later.

edges.label: The Tripura brothers were devout worshippers of Shiva until they were led astray (Shiva Purana)
Vishnu became Shiva's arrow and, in the Shiva Purana, sent a heretical teacher to lead the brothers from dharma
Vishnu as Gadadhara stood on the stone over Gaya and held him still forever — a subjugation, not a killing, in the Vayu Purana
edges.variation: Popular retellings say Vishnu pushed him into the netherworld or killed him with his mace.

edges.label: Vishnu made Gaya's body holier than all tirthas and granted that offerings at Gaya liberate the ancestors
Gaya was a great devotee of Vishnu
Yama protested that Gaya's liberating holiness had emptied his realm
Gaya gladly gave his body as the ground for Brahma's sacrifice
Rambha and Karambha were sons of Danu (Devi Bhagavata)
Agni stopped Rambha's self-sacrifice and granted him an invincible, shape-shifting son (Devi Bhagavata)
Indra, as a crocodile, killed Rambha's brother Karambha during his austerities
Brahma granted Mahishi that only a son born of Shiva and Vishnu could kill her
edges.variation: Kerala regional tradition.

edges.label: Dattatreya cursed his wife Leela to be born as the buffalo-demoness Mahishi
edges.variation: Sabarimala tradition; freed by Ayyappa she became Malikappurathamma.

edges.label: Jaya and Vijaya are brothers and joint doorkeepers of Vaikuntha
Ravana was the second birth of Jaya (Bhagavata 7.1)
edges.variation: Individual mapping is conventional; some retellings make Ravana Vijaya.

edges.label: Shishupala was the third birth of Jaya (Bhagavata 7.1)
edges.variation: Individual mapping is conventional; Dantavakra is the other brother's third birth.

edges.label: Kumbhakarna was the second birth of Vijaya (Bhagavata 7.1)
edges.variation: Individual mapping is conventional; some retellings make Kumbhakarna Jaya.

edges.label: Bhrigu is one of the mind-born sons (Manasaputras) of Brahma (Vishnu Purana 1.7)
edges.variation: Vedic texts make him Bhrigu Varuni, son of Varuna; the Mahabharata says he was born from the fire of Varuna's sacrifice

edges.label: Chyavana was born to Bhrigu and Puloma; his radiance burned the rakshasa who carried off his mother (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 5–6)
Bhrigu → Chyavana → Aurva → Richika → Jamadagni (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Parashurama, 'Rama of the Bhrigus', is the most famous Bhargava
Markandeya, son of Mrikandu, belongs to Bhrigu's lineage (Vishnu Purana 1.10)
Bhrigu, Daksha's son-in-law through Khyati, took Daksha's side against Shiva at the sacrifice (Bhagavata Purana 4.2–4.5)
Atri is a mind-born son of Brahma (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 65; Vishnu Purana 1.7)
Atri and Anasuya, the ideal ascetic couple of Chitrakuta
Durvasa, a portion of Shiva, was born to Atri and Anasuya (Bhagavata Purana 4.1)
Pleased by Atri's tapas on Mount Riksha, Vishnu, Brahma and Shiva appeared together and promised to be born as his sons (Bhagavata Purana 4.1)
The Ashvins rescued Atri from a burning chasm and cooled it for him (Rig Veda 1.116.8, 1.117.3)
Atri restored the Sun after the asura Svarbhanu had pierced it with darkness (Rig Veda 5.40)
edges.variation: Later tradition identifies Svarbhanu with Rahu

edges.label: Atri welcomed Rama, Sita and Lakshmana at his hermitage (Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda)
Durvasa is the son of Anasuya and Atri (Bhagavata Purana 4.1)
Anasuya gave Sita a celestial garland, garments, ornaments and an unguent that would never fade (Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda)
Kashyapa is the son of Marichi (Ramayana 1.70; Mahabharata, Adi Parva 65)
Kadru, daughter of Daksha, is the wife of Kashyapa and mother of the Nagas
Vinata, daughter of Daksha, is the wife of Kashyapa and mother of Aruna and Garuda
Garuda is the son of Kashyapa and Vinata (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Aruna, charioteer of the Sun, is the son of Kashyapa and Vinata (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Shesha is the eldest of the Nagas born to Kashyapa and Kadru (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Vasuki is a Naga son of Kashyapa and Kadru (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Takshaka is a Naga son of Kashyapa and Kadru (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Angiras is a mind-born son of Brahma (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 65; Vishnu Purana 1.7)
edges.variation: In the Rig Veda the Angirases are a clan of ancestral priests

edges.label: The Angirases sang open the Vala cave with Indra and freed the cows and the light (Rig Veda 1.62; 10.108)
Agni is called the first of the Angirases (Rig Veda 1.1.6, 1.31.1); the Mahabharata tells how Angiras once took over Agni's role
Bharadvaja, son of Brihaspati, is a grandson of Angiras
The Gautamas are a branch of the Angirasa clan in the gotra lists
Kacha, son of Brihaspati, is a grandson of Angiras
Pulastya is a mind-born son of Brahma (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 65; Vishnu Purana 1.7)
Vishrava was born to Pulastya and Trinabindu's daughter (Ramayana, Uttara Kanda 2)
Ravana is Pulastya's grandson through Vishrava, hence the name Paulastya
Kubera is Pulastya's grandson through Vishrava (Ramayana, Uttara Kanda 3)
Kumbhakarna is Pulastya's grandson through Vishrava
Vibhishana is Pulastya's grandson through Vishrava
Because Parashara gave up his sacrifice to destroy the rakshasas, Pulastya blessed him to compose a Purana (Vishnu Purana 1.1)
Pulastya taught Bhishma the merits of pilgrimage to the tirthas (Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Tirthayatra section)
The Bhagavata (4.1) names Agastya a son of Pulastya and Havirbhu
edges.variation: The Rig Veda and the epics say Agastya was born of Mitra and Varuna in a jar

edges.label: Pulastya and Pulaha are brothers among Brahma's mind-born sons and are usually named together
Pulaha is a mind-born son of Brahma, born from his navel in the Bhagavata (3.12)
The Vishnu Purana (1.10) makes Kardama a son of Pulaha and Kshama
edges.variation: The Bhagavata says Kardama was born from Brahma's shadow and makes Pulaha his son-in-law through Gati

edges.label: Pulaha and Kratu are brothers among Brahma's mind-born sons
Kratu is a mind-born son of Brahma (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 65; Vishnu Purana 1.7)
Kratu and Marichi are brothers among Brahma's mind-born sons
Marichi is usually named first among Brahma's mind-born sons (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 65; Vishnu Purana 1.7)
Brahma → Marichi → Kashyapa → Vivasvan → Manu, at the head of the Ikshvaku genealogy (Ramayana 1.70)
The Bhagavad Gita (10.21) names Marichi as chief of the Maruts
edges.variation: Many commentators take this Marichi to be a different figure from the Prajapati

edges.label: Vashistha is a mind-born son of Brahma in the Puranas (Vishnu Purana 1.7)
edges.variation: The Rig Veda has him born of Mitra and Varuna; the Puranas reconcile the two by a second birth after Nimi's curse

edges.label: Vashistha and Arundhati, the model couple, are shown to brides as the stars Mizar and Alcor
Shakti (Shaktri) is the eldest of Vashistha's hundred sons (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Parashara is Vashistha's grandson through Shakti, raised by Vashistha after Shakti's death
Vyasa is Vashistha's great-grandson: Vashistha → Shakti → Parashara → Vyasa
The feud between Vashistha and Vishvamitra over the wish-fulfilling cow, and over brahmin against kshatriya power (Ramayana 1.51–56; Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
edges.variation: The Rig Veda shows both sages as rival priests of King Sudas (Mandalas 3 and 7)

edges.label: Vashistha is Rama's family guru and teacher (Ramayana; framed as his teacher in the Yoga Vasishtha)
Vashistha guided Bharata after Dasharatha's death and during Rama's exile (Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda)
Vashistha is Dasharatha's purohita (royal priest) and adviser
Vashistha has been purohita of the Ikshvaku line since its founder (Ramayana, Uttara Kanda)
Nandini is Vashistha's wish-fulfilling cow, whom Vishvamitra tried to seize (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
edges.variation: In the Ramayana the cow is called Shabala

edges.label: Vashistha branded Satyavrata with three sins (tri-shanku), which gave him his name (Harivamsha 1.13)
edges.variation: In the Ramayana (1.58) it is Vashistha's sons who curse Trishanku to become an outcaste

edges.label: Both were born from the seed of Mitra and Varuna in a jar at the sight of Urvashi (Rig Veda 7.33.13)
Arundhati is the mother of Shakti, eldest son of Vashistha
The Shiva Purana says Arundhati was once Sandhya, a mind-born daughter of Brahma, reborn as the daughter of Medhatithi
Pleased by Arundhati's tapas during a twelve-year drought, Shiva blessed her and made the place a tirtha, Badarapachana (Mahabharata, Shalya Parva)
Vishvamitra taught Rama the Bala and Atibala mantras and gave him divine astras (Ramayana, Bala Kanda)
Vishvamitra took Lakshmana, with Rama, to guard his sacrifice and taught them both (Ramayana, Bala Kanda)
Vishvamitra sent Trishanku to heaven in his own body and made a new heaven of stars when Indra pushed him back (Ramayana 1.57–60)
Vishvamitra taught Shunahshepa the hymns that freed him from being sacrificed (Ramayana 1.61–62)
edges.variation: In the Aitareya Brahmana (7.13–18) Vishvamitra adopts him as his eldest son, Devarata

edges.label: Shakuntala is the daughter of Vishvamitra and the apsara Menaka (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Vishvamitra cursed Rambha, sent by Indra to seduce him, to become a rock for ten thousand years (Ramayana 1.64)
Vishvamitra stripped Harishchandra of kingdom, family and freedom to test his truthfulness (Markandeya Purana 7–8)
edges.variation: The ordeal is a test and ends in Harishchandra's vindication; the Aitareya Brahmana's version does not include it

edges.label: Maricha disrupted Vishvamitra's sacrifice until Rama drove him away (Ramayana, Bala Kanda)
Subahu disrupted Vishvamitra's sacrifice and was killed by Rama (Ramayana, Bala Kanda)
Vishvamitra sent a rakshasa into King Kalmashapada, who then devoured Vashistha's son Shakti (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
When Jamadagni aimed arrows at the Sun for scorching Renuka, Surya calmed him with the first umbrella and sandals (Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva)
In later tellings, Jamadagni's hermitage cow, coveted by Kartavirya, is Kamadhenu
edges.variation: The Mahabharata speaks only of the calf of his homa-dhenu (sacrificial cow)

edges.label: Ahalya is the wife of Gautama (Ramayana, Bala Kanda)
Gautama cursed Ahalya to live unseen in his hermitage until Rama came (Ramayana 1.48)
edges.variation: In later tellings she is turned to stone

edges.label: Kripa, born to Sharadvan son of Gautama, bears the name Gautama (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Kripi, Kripa's twin, was born to Sharadvan, son of Gautama (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Shiva released the Ganga onto Brahmagiri as the Godavari (Gautami) for Gautama (Brahma Purana, Gautami Mahatmya)
Indra seduced Ahalya disguised as Gautama (Shatapatha Brahmana 3.3.4.18; Ramayana 1.48)
edges.variation: No edge type fits exactly. In Valmiki's Bala Kanda Ahalya knowingly consents; in the Uttara Kanda and later texts she is deceived

edges.label: Rama's arrival at Gautama's hermitage ended Ahalya's curse (Ramayana 1.49)
edges.variation: In the Adhyatma Ramayana and Ramcharitmanas, the touch of Rama's foot brings her back from stone

edges.label: In some regional and Southeast Asian Ramayanas (e.g. the Thai Ramakien), Anjana is a daughter of Gautama and Ahalya
Drona was born in a vessel (drona) from Bharadvaja's seed, shed at the sight of the apsara Ghritachi (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Indra taught Bharadvaja the endlessness of the Veda (Taittiriya Brahmana 3.10.11) and the science of Ayurveda (Charaka Samhita, Sutrasthana 1)
Bharadvaja hosted Rama at Prayaga and directed him to Chitrakuta (Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 54)
Bharadvaja feasted Bharata's whole army through his ascetic power (Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 91)
Bharadvaja is Kubera's maternal grandfather: his daughter Devavarnini (Ilavida) married Vishrava (Ramayana, Uttara Kanda 3)
A disciple named Bharadvaja goes with Valmiki at the opening of the Ramayana (1.2)
edges.variation: It is unclear whether this disciple is the Vedic seer

edges.label: The Maruts gave the abandoned infant Bharadvaja to King Bharata, who adopted him (Vishnu Purana 4.19; Bhagavata 9.20)
The Ashvins gave Dadhyanch a horse's head so that he could teach them without breaking Indra's threat (Shatapatha Brahmana 14.1.1)
Dadhichi gave up his life so that his bones could become Indra's vajra (Rig Veda 1.84.13; Mahabharata, Vana Parva 100; Bhagavata 6.10)
Shaiva Puranas praise Dadhichi as a great devotee of Shiva (Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
Dadhichi rebuked Daksha for leaving Shiva out of the sacrifice and walked out (Shiva Purana, Rudra Samhita)
The Linga Purana tells of Dadhichi defeating Vishnu in a dispute over King Kshuva
edges.variation: This is a Shaiva sectarian episode not found in Vaishnava texts

edges.label: King Sharyati gave his daughter Sukanya to Chyavana after she blinded him by mistake (Shatapatha Brahmana 4.1.5)
Chyavana won the Ashvins a share of soma at Sharyati's sacrifice (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 124)
When Indra raised the vajra against him, Chyavana froze his arm and conjured the demon Mada (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 124)
Chyavana → Aurva → Richika → Jamadagni (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
Pleased by King Kushika's patience, Chyavana foretold that Kushika's grandson Vishvamitra would become a brahmin (Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva)
King Nahusha ransomed Chyavana from fishermen, valuing him as highly as a cow (Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva)
Some Puranas make Dadhicha a son of Chyavana and Sukanya
edges.variation: The Rig Veda calls Dadhyanch a son of Atharvan

edges.label: Sukanya is the daughter of Sharyati, son of Manu (Shatapatha Brahmana 4.1.5; Bhagavata 9.3)
The Ashvins tried to win Sukanya; she stayed faithful and in return told them how to gain their place at the sacrifice (Shatapatha Brahmana 4.1.5)
In Puranic genealogies Jamadagni descends from Chyavana and Sukanya through Apnavana, Aurva and Richika
edges.variation: The Mahabharata names Arushi, not Sukanya, as Aurva's mother

edges.label: Agastya and Lopamudra, who speak together in Rig Veda 1.179
Agastya created Lopamudra from the finest features of all creatures and gave her to the king of Vidarbha to raise (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 94)
Agastya gave Rama Vishnu's bow, inexhaustible quivers and a sword (Ramayana 3.12) and taught him the Aditya Hridaya
edges.variation: The Aditya Hridaya is in the vulgate Yuddha Kanda but not in the Critical Edition

edges.label: Agastya cursed the arrogant Nahusha, who had become Indra, to fall to earth as a serpent (Mahabharata, Udyoga and Anushasana Parvas)
edges.variation: In the Anushasana Parva, Bhrigu, hidden in Agastya's matted hair, speaks the curse

edges.label: Agastya cursed Tataka to become a man-eating rakshasi (Ramayana 1.25)
Agastya cursed Maricha, Tataka's son, to become a rakshasa (Ramayana 1.25)
Agastya drank the ocean dry so that Indra and the gods could destroy the Kalakeya asuras hiding in it (Mahabharata, Vana Parva)
Narada is a mind-born son of Brahma; the Bhagavata says he sprang from Brahma's lap
Narada is the archetypal devotee of Vishnu-Narayana, ever chanting his name
Narada told Valmiki the story of Rama, the seed of the Ramayana (Bala Kanda 1)
Narada taught the boy Dhruva to meditate on Vishnu with the twelve-syllable mantra (Bhagavata 4.8)
edges.variation: In the Vishnu Purana the Saptarishi instruct Dhruva instead.

edges.label: Narada urged the dissatisfied Vyasa to compose the Bhagavata, singing Krishna's glories (Bhagavata 1.5)
Narada instructed Shuka before his final liberation (Mahabharata, Shanti Parva)
With Vishvamitra and Kanva, Narada cursed Samba, disguised as a pregnant woman, to bear the iron club that destroyed the Yadavas (Mausala Parva)
Narada instructed Yudhishthira on kingship in his new assembly hall (Sabha Parva 5) and told the Pandavas the tale of Sunda and Upasunda
Narada warned that Satyavan would die within a year, yet Savitri held to her choice (Vana Parva)
Narada rescued the pregnant Kayadhu from Indra and sheltered her in his hermitage (Bhagavata 7.7)
Narada and the gandharva Tumburu are paired celestial musicians, at times rivals in song
Narada advised the sonless Harishchandra to pray to Varuna for a son (Aitareya Brahmana 7.13)
Durvasa was born of a portion (amsha) of Shiva, as Dattatreya was of Vishnu and Soma of Brahma
Brothers, sons of Atri and Anasuya in the Bhagavata's account
edges.variation: Elsewhere Soma is born from Atri's eyes or from the churning of the ocean.

edges.label: Durvasa cursed the distracted Shakuntala to be forgotten by Dushyanta until he saw a token
edges.variation: Kalidasa's Abhijnanashakuntalam; absent from the Mahabharata version.

edges.label: Pleased by the young Kunti's service, Durvasa gave her a mantra to summon any god and have a child by him (Adi Parva)
Durvasa, offended, sent a demon against King Ambarisha; Vishnu's Sudarshana pursued him until he begged Ambarisha's forgiveness (Bhagavata 9.4–5)
Pleased by Duryodhana's hospitality, Durvasa granted a boon; Duryodhana asked him to visit the exiled Pandavas after Draupadi had eaten (Vana Parva)
After Krishna and Rukmini served him patiently, Durvasa blessed Krishna's body with invulnerability wherever it had been smeared with his payasa (Anushasana Parva)
edges.variation: Later tradition links the unsmeared sole to the hunter Jara's fatal arrow.

edges.label: Durvasa's hungry arrival at the forest hermitage tested Draupadi; Krishna ate a morsel from her pot and the sage and his disciples felt sated and left (Vana Parva)
Parashara fathered Vyasa on Satyavati on an island in the Yamuna (Adi Parva 1.57)
Satyavati bore Krishna Dvaipayana on an island (dvipa) before her marriage to Shantanu
Biological father by niyoga with Ambika, at Satyavati's request after Vichitravirya died childless; Dhritarashtra was born blind because Ambika shut her eyes
Biological father by niyoga with Ambalika; Pandu was born pale because she turned pale at the sight of the sage
Biological father by niyoga with a maidservant sent in Ambika's place, who received him calmly and bore the wise Vidura
Shuka was born from Vyasa's seed fallen on the fire-sticks (Shanti Parva)
Vyasa taught the Mahabharata and the Yajurveda to his disciple Vaishampayana
Vyasa taught Shuka the Vedas and the Mahabharata
Vyasa granted Sanjaya divine sight to narrate the Kurukshetra war to Dhritarashtra (Bhishma Parva)
Pleased by Gandhari's hospitality, Vyasa granted her a hundred sons (Adi Parva)
Half-brothers, both sons of Satyavati; Vyasa raised heirs for the childless Vichitravirya
Vyasa worshipped Shiva on Mount Meru and received the boon of a son as pure as the elements (Shanti Parva)
Vyasa is named among the Saptarishi of the coming eighth (Savarni) manvantara (Vishnu Purana 3.2)
Vyasa repeatedly counselled Yudhishthira: consoling him after the war and urging the ashvamedha sacrifice (Shanti and Ashvamedhika Parvas)
Vyasa explained to Drupada that Draupadi's marriage to five husbands was ordained by her past life (Adi Parva)

edges.variation: South Indian temple legend.

edges.label: Lakshmana anointed Vibhishana king and was guided by him to Nikumbhila
Vibhishana revealed the secret of Indrajit's Nikumbhila rite, leading to his death
Several later retellings make Trijata Vibhishana's daughter
edges.variation: Kamba Ramayanam and some later tellings; Valmiki gives her no parentage; the Thai Ramakien makes her his wife.

edges.label: Mandodari bore Meghanada (Indrajit)
Many retellings name Mandodari as Aksha's mother
edges.variation: Valmiki does not name his mother.

edges.label: Folk legend: Parvati cursed the apsara Madhura to be a frog, later restored as Mandodari
edges.variation: Regional/folk tradition only.

edges.label: Through the Maheshvara sacrifice Indrajit won a sky-chariot and the power of illusion from Shiva (Pashupati)
Shukracharya (Ushanas) officiated the seven great sacrifices of Meghanada
Indrajit twice felled Rama and his army with the serpent-noose and the Brahmastra
Garuda freed Rama and Lakshmana from Indrajit's serpent arrows
Indrajit and Atikaya were sons of Ravana
Indrajit went out to avenge his slain brother Aksha
Kaikesi was Shurpanakha's mother
edges.variation: Mahabharata's Ramopakhyana names her mother Raka.

edges.label: Khara, lord of Janasthana, was Shurpanakha's brother and protector
edges.variation: Uttara Kanda makes him a maternal cousin; Mahabharata makes them twins.

edges.label: Tataka was Maricha's mother; his father was the yaksha Sunda
Tataka was Subahu's mother
Maricha and Subahu, sons of Tataka, together defiled Vishvamitra's sacrifices
As the golden deer Maricha lured Rama away so that Sita could be abducted
Lakshmana guarded Vishvamitra's sacrifice against Subahu's band
Vishvamitra led Rama to destroy Tataka, who had ravaged Malada and Karusha
Lakshmana cut off Tataka's nose and ears in the fight
Khara was Ravana's kinsman and governor of Janasthana
edges.variation: Aranya Kanda calls him Ravana's brother; Uttara Kanda makes him son of Kaikesi's sister Raka.

edges.label: Dushana commanded Khara's army of fourteen thousand
Khara's army came to avenge Lakshmana's mutilation of Shurpanakha
Dushana marched to avenge Shurpanakha
Dushana helped hold Janasthana, Ravana's frontier outpost
Sumali was the father of Prahasta (Uttara Kanda)
Prahasta and Kaikesi were children of Sumali
Prahasta clashed with Vibhishana in Ravana's war council
Brahma gave Atikaya impenetrable armour and divine weapons
Atikaya and Aksha were sons of Ravana
Atikaya rode against Rama's army after Kumbhakarna's fall
Sarama and Trijata were Sita's two protectors in Lanka
Ramcharitmanas presents Trijata as a devotee of Rama
edges.variation: Valmiki shows her respect for Rama and Sita; devotional framing is later.

edges.label: Sumali was Kaikesi's father
Regional legend makes Kaikesi a devout Shiva worshipper
edges.variation: Gokarna Atmalinga legend; not in Valmiki.

edges.label: Brahma granted Sumali and his brothers invincibility and brotherly unity
Vishnu slew Mali and drove Sumali's rakshasas from Lanka into Patala
Vishvakarma directed Sumali and his brothers to Lanka, the city he had built on Trikuta
The Vasu Savitra killed Sumali in Ravana's war with the gods
Sumali urged his grandson Ravana to reclaim Lanka from Kubera
Sumali schemed to recover Lanka from Kubera
Vedavati did penance to win Vishnu as her husband
Vedavati was the granddaughter of Brihaspati through the brahmarshi Kushadhvaja
The Devi Bhagavata Purana calls Vedavati a portion of Lakshmi
edges.variation: Devi Bhagavata Purana, Book 9; not in Valmiki.

edges.label: Brahmavaivarta Purana: Vedavati, having served as the illusory Sita, was later reborn as Draupadi
edges.variation: Brahmavaivarta Purana only.

edges.label: Manu passed the eternal yoga, received from Vivasvan, on to Ikshvaku (Bhagavad Gita 4.1)
Mandhata, son of Yuvanashva, descends from Ikshvaku
edges.variation: Puranic line: Ikshvaku - Vikukshi - Kakutstha - ... - Yuvanashva - Mandhata. Valmiki's list is Ikshvaku - Kukshi - Vikukshi - Bana - Anaranya - Prithu - Trishanku - Dhundhumara - Yuvanashva - Mandhata

edges.label: Through his son Nimi, Ikshvaku is ancestor of the Janakas of Videha (Puranas)
edges.variation: Vishnu Purana 4.5 and the Bhagavata make Nimi Ikshvaku's son. Valmiki starts Janaka's genealogy from Nimi without linking him to Ikshvaku

edges.label: Trishanku (Satyavrata), son of Trayyaruna, descends from Mandhata through Purukutsa
edges.variation: Valmiki's genealogy reverses this and puts Trishanku before Mandhata

edges.label: Indra fed the newborn Mandhata from his own finger and gave him his name ('he shall suckle me')
The Rig Veda (1.112.13) praises the Ashvins for helping Mandhatri
Vishnu, appearing in the form of Indra, taught Mandhata the duties of kings (Mahabharata, Shanti Parva 64–65)
Harishchandra was the son of Trishanku (Satyavrata)
edges.variation: The Aitareya Brahmana calls Harishchandra the son of Vedhas (Vaidhasa). Valmiki's genealogy has no Harishchandra

edges.label: Vishvamitra became Trishanku's priest, sent him up bodily toward heaven, and created a new heaven of stars for him
Indra threw Trishanku out of heaven head first, refusing him entry in his mortal body
Rohita was born to Harishchandra by Varuna's grace (Aitareya Brahmana)
Taramati (Shaivya) was Harishchandra's queen and shared his ordeal of truth
Vishvamitra was hotr priest at Harishchandra's sacrifice (Aitareya Brahmana). In the Puranas he tests the king's truthfulness by stripping him of everything
edges.variation: The ordeal of truth comes from the Markandeya and Devi Bhagavata Puranas

edges.label: Vashishtha was Harishchandra's family priest and brahman priest at the Shunahshepa sacrifice. He took the king's side against Vishvamitra (Markandeya Purana)
After the ordeal, Indra and the gods raised Harishchandra to heaven together with his subjects (Markandeya Purana)
Dharma, who had disguised himself as the chandala master, revealed the test and blessed Harishchandra
edges.variation: The Markandeya Purana names Dharma personified. Identifying Dharma with Yama is traditional but not explicit in the text

edges.label: Shaivya (Taramati) was the mother of Rohita(shva), whose death and revival end the ordeal
Indra, in human form, urged the wandering Rohita each year to keep moving ('charaiveti')
Rohita bought Shunahshepa for a hundred cows to be sacrificed in his place
Sagara descends from Rohita through Harita, Champa, Sudeva, Vijaya, Bharuka, Vrika and Bahu (Puranas)
edges.variation: Valmiki has no Rohita. There Sagara is the son of Asita, in the line of Mandhata's descendants

edges.label: Vishvamitra adopted the freed Shunahshepa as his eldest son, renaming him Devarata
edges.variation: Adoptive father. His birth father was Ajigarta (Aitareya Brahmana) or Richika (Valmiki)

edges.label: As Shunahshepa praised Ushas, his fetters loosened verse by verse and fell away (Aitareya Brahmana)
Shunahshepa praised Agni in several of his hymns of deliverance
Shunahshepa praised Savitr, who sent him on to Varuna
Shunahshepa first turned to Prajapati, who sent him on to Agni
In the Valmiki Ramayana, Indra, pleased by the hymns Vishvamitra taught him, frees Shunahshepa
edges.variation: Valmiki (Bala Kanda 62): the hymns are to Indra and Upendra, and the king is Ambarisha

edges.label: Asamanja was Sagara's son by Queen Keshini
Bhrigu granted Sagara one son to continue his line by one queen and sixty thousand sons by the other (Valmiki)
The Bhargava Chyavana blessed Sagara's mother, and the child was born safely despite the poison given her (Valmiki)
edges.variation: In the Puranas the sage who protects the mother and raises Sagara is Aurva

edges.label: Indra stole Sagara's sacrificial horse and hid it in the underworld beside Kapila
Vashishtha persuaded Sagara to spare the conquered Shakas, Yavanas and others and impose distinctive dress on them instead (Vishnu Purana)
Kapila burned Sagara's sixty thousand sons to ashes when they attacked him as the horse-thief
Anshuman was Asamanja's son and became Sagara's heir
Dilipa was the son of Anshuman
Garuda, brother of Queen Sumati, told Anshuman that only the Ganga could purify the ashes (Valmiki)
Bhagiratha was the son of Dilipa, son of Anshuman
Vashishtha told the childless Dilipa to serve the cow Nandini (Raghuvamsha)
edges.variation: This concerns Kalidasa's Dilipa, father of Raghu, usually taken as a later king than Bhagiratha's father

edges.label: Surabhi cursed Dilipa to be childless after he passed her without saluting her (Raghuvamsha)
edges.variation: Kalidasa's Dilipa

edges.label: Dilipa served Nandini as a cowherd and offered his own body to a lion to save her, and she granted him a son
edges.variation: Kalidasa's Raghuvamsha, cantos 1–2

edges.label: Raghu descends from Bhagiratha in the Solar line
edges.variation: Valmiki: Bhagiratha - Kakutstha - Raghu. The Vishnu Purana and Bhagavata put Raghu several generations later, as son of Dirghabahu, son of Khatvanga-Dilipa. Kalidasa makes Raghu the son of Dilipa and Sudakshina

edges.label: Pleased by his austerities at Gokarna, Brahma granted Bhagiratha the descent of the Ganga
Shiva caught the falling Ganga in his locks and released her in streams at Bhagiratha's request
Aja was the son of Raghu (Kalidasa, Vishnu Purana)
edges.variation: Valmiki's genealogy makes Aja the son of Nabhaga, several generations after Raghu

edges.label: Kubera rained gold into Raghu's treasury overnight so that he could pay Kautsa's fee (Raghuvamsha)
Young Raghu fought Indra to recover Dilipa's stolen sacrificial horse (Raghuvamsha, canto 3)
edges.variation: Indra, impressed, granted him the merit of the sacrifice though he kept the horse

edges.label: Vashishtha served as Raghu's family priest
Indumati chose Aja at her svayamvara in Vidarbha (Raghuvamsha)
Vashishtha consoled the grieving Aja, revealing that Indumati had been a cursed apsara (Raghuvamsha, canto 8)
In the Valmiki Ramayana, King Ila is the son of Kardama Prajapati
edges.variation: Uttara Kanda 87. Other texts make Ila Manu's child

edges.label: Budha, son of the Moon, fell in love with Ila while she was in female form
Vashishtha turned Manu's daughter Ila into the son Sudyumna and later interceded with Shiva for him
Shiva's decree that any man entering his grove would become female turned Sudyumna into Ila
At Vashishtha's plea, Shiva allowed Sudyumna to be a man one month and a woman the next (Bhagavata)
In the Ramayana, Uma granted half of Ila's plea, so that he would be a man and a woman in alternate months
Ila bore Pururavas to Budha, so the Lunar line is called Aila
Pururavas was the son of Budha, son of Soma
The apsara Urvashi lived with Pururavas on conditions, left him, and returned to him once a year (Rig Veda 10.95)
Ayu was the eldest son of Pururavas and Urvashi
Pururavas kindled the sacred fire with the fire-drills and established it in threefold form (Shatapatha Brahmana, Bhagavata)
Pururavas fought for Indra's side and rescued Urvashi from the demon Keshin (Vikramorvashiyam)
edges.variation: Found in Kalidasa's play and later sources

edges.label: Urvashi was the mother of Ayu
Nahusha was the eldest son of Ayu
Dattatreya, pleased by Ayu's patient service, blessed him with a son, Nahusha (Padma Purana)
Yayati was the son of Nahusha
Hidden in Agastya's matted hair, Bhrigu cursed the arrogant Nahusha (Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva)
edges.variation: Most versions give the curse to Agastya alone

Yudhishthira's answers to the python's questions ended Nahusha's curse and freed Bhima
Yayati pulled Devayani out of a well by her right hand and married her
Yayati secretly married Sharmishtha, Devayani's servant, and fathered three sons with her
Yadu was Yayati's eldest son, born of Devayani
Puru was Yayati's youngest son, born of Sharmishtha
Shukracharya relented enough to let Yayati pass his old age to a willing son

Devayani was the mother of Yadu and Turvasu
Devayani and Sharmishtha quarrelled bitterly; Sharmishtha threw her into a well and later had to serve her

Sharmishtha was the mother of Druhyu, Anu and Puru

Yadu and Puru were half-brothers, sons of Yayati by Devayani and Sharmishtha
Shurasena, grandfather of Krishna, descends from Yadu through Kroshtu and the Vrishnis
Dushyanta was a king of the Paurava line founded by Puru

edges.label: Dushyanta married Shakuntala by the gandharva rite in Kanva's hermitage
Bharata (Sarvadamana) was the son of Dushyanta and Shakuntala
Dushyanta fought the demons on Indra's behalf (Abhijnanashakuntalam, Act 7)
edges.variation: From Kalidasa's play, not the Mahabharata

edges.label: The sage Marica (Kashyapa) reunited Dushyanta with Shakuntala and their son in his celestial hermitage and blessed them (Kalidasa)
edges.variation: From Kalidasa's play, not the Mahabharata

Kanva found the abandoned infant, named her, and raised her in his hermitage as a foster-daughter
Shakuntala raised Bharata in Kanva's hermitage and presented him at Dushyanta's court
Kuru, son of Samvarana, descends from Bharata through Bhumanyu, Suhotra, Hastin and Ajamidha

Pratipa, father of Shantanu, descends from Kuru
Indra granted Kuru that all who die on the field he ploughed would reach heaven, and so it became Kurukshetra
Kuru's mother Tapati was the daughter of Surya, so Surya was his maternal grandfather (Adi Parva)
Pratipa belongs to the Paurava line founded by Puru, son of Yayati
Pratipa fathered Shantanu in old age and promised Ganga to him as a bride

Satyavati bore Vichitravirya to Shantanu

Half-brothers: Bhishma ruled as regent for Vichitravirya and won his brides

Sisters, princesses of Kashi, both married to Vichitravirya

Draupadi's husband and protector, who killed Kichaka and Dushasana for her sake
